scenario: A technician wearing smart glasses repairs an ATV (all-terrain vehicle) in a workshop, removing and reinstalling parts with hand tools while a remote expert guides them.

questions.ask: Does this video itself show a hand tool turning a visible ATV fastener to loosen it, not merely being held against the fastener?
questions.why: Shows a common first step in removing ATV parts.

questions.ask: Does this video itself show a body or access panel being lifted away from the ATV, not merely being touched or wiggled while still attached?
Does this video itself show a removed ATV fastener being placed in a tray or container, not simply set down on the work surface?
questions.why: Helps spot whether removed hardware is being kept together.

questions.ask: Does this video itself show an electrical connector being separated at its plug, not merely a wire being moved or handled?
questions.why: Tracks disconnection before work on electrical parts.

questions.ask: Does this video itself show a hand pulling directly on wires to disconnect a plug, not gripping the connector housing?
questions.why: Identifies a visible way wiring can be damaged.

questions.ask: Does this video itself show an ATV wheel being pulled off its hub, not merely being rotated while still mounted?
questions.why: Tracks a common repair access step.

questions.ask: Does this video itself show an ATV wheel being placed onto its hub, not merely held near the hub?
Does this video itself show liquid visibly dripping or pooling beneath an opened ATV component, not just a wet or oily surface already present?
questions.why: Flags a visible fluid leak or spill during repair.
